newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Typhoon Winnie kills 13 in Taiwan, heads for China.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Winnie kills 13 in Taiwan, heads for China.

text.p: Typhoon Winnie, the first storm to hit Taiwan this year, caused landslides, collapsed buildings and flooded streets on Monday, killing at least 13 people, officials and state media said.
Police reported 13 people were killed and one missing. But State radio said the death toll had risen to 20 as Winnie swept across the north and northeastern parts of Taiwan.
At 1000 GMT, Winnie was 260 km (162 miles) north-northeast of Taipei and moving west-northwest at 25 kph (16 mph), the Central Weather Bureau said.
The storm was expected to hit China on Monday evening.
"Winnie's strength is weakening and is expected to land in China's coastal areas in the evening," a weather forecaster told state radio.
Heavy torrential rain and strong winds triggered landslides in Taipei, destroying or damaging buildings and blocking traffic.
At least 10 five-storey buildings in a mountainous area in eastern Taipei collapsed, killing six and injuring 25, state media reported.
"The whole scene looks as if it has gone through an explosion," said a state television reporter at the scene.
Local authorities mobilised hundreds of rescue workers and soldiers to help evacuate residents, but several people remained trapped in their houses, state media said.
Seven people were buried after landslides hit their house in north Taipei. Only one woman survived.
Torrential rain swamped houses in low-lying areas of the capital, Taipei. Many roads were flooded and scores of vehicles submerged.
The typhoon, packing maximum sustained winds of 144 km per hour (89 miles per hour) and gusts of up to 180 kph (112 mph), forced government agencies, financial markets and schools to close on Monday.
All domestic flights were cancelled but most international flights were running to schedule. Many roads in mountainous areas were impassable.
Some 68,500 households suffered power shortages, officials said.
